comment: Pinned OpenList release the embedded Android runtime is taken from.
Desktop hosts keep downloading the same pinned release at first use; Android never downloads.
The Android payload is now built from the pinned source tag (android.build) instead of the
official release asset: the official v4.2.6 Android build passes only -tags=jsoniter, so its
GORM SQLite driver is the pure-Go glebarez/modernc stack, and modernc.org/libc v1.22.5 calls the
raw lstat syscall (x86_64 syscall 6) which the Android app seccomp filter rejects. Admin
initialization therefore dies with SIGSYS before the server starts. The source build keeps the
same tag and adds the project's own sqlite_cgo_compat tag, selecting github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3
compiled by the NDK against Bionic libc (Bionic implements stat/lstat through fstatat, which
apps are allowed to call), and links with 16 KB page alignment.
Payload integrity stays on the pinned version plus official HTTPS origins (OpenList source tag,
OpenList-Frontend release, NDK); no extra checksum scheme is introduced.

android.sourceNote: Built from the pinned OpenList v4.2.6 source tag with the official build.sh settings (GOOS=android, NDK *-linux-android24-clang, CGO_ENABLED=1, llvm-strip) plus -tags=jsoniter,sqlite_cgo_compat and -Wl,-z,max-page-size=16384.

build.sqliteDriverEvidence: The built payload must report a github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3 dependency and no modernc.org/* dependency in `go version -m`; that is what proves the raw-lstat driver is gone.

frontend.note: The same frontend release build.sh FetchWebRelease embedded for the official v4.2.6 build (newest non-lite dist on 2026-09-01); pinned here so the source build keeps the admin web UI.
